**Overlap metrics and semantic metrics notice different kinds of agreement.** BLEU uses clipped n-gram precision with a brevity penalty, rewarding generated phrases that appear in references. ROUGE variants emphasize overlap through recall, subsequences, or related formulas. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

A valid paraphrase can receive low lexical overlap. BERTScore compares contextual token representations, and MoverScore uses a transport-style alignment, making them more tolerant of some paraphrases.

**Semantic closeness is not factual equivalence.** “The shipment contains 15 units” and “the shipment contains 50 units” are similar sentences with a crucial numerical disagreement. Negation and unsupported details can be missed by both broad semantic matching and aggregate overlap scores.

Use metrics as complementary diagnostics, with exact variants and tokenization specified. Corpus-level BLEU is not interchangeable with a single sentence's score. For summarization, check claims against the source and assess missing important information as well as invented content. Multiple references can recognize legitimate wording variation, but no one automatic score establishes faithfulness or usefulness by itself.

**Technical details and references.**

BLEU measures clipped n-gram precision with a brevity penalty, often aggregated at corpus level. ROUGE variants emphasize reference overlap through recall, longest common subsequences, or related formulations. BERTScore compares contextual token embeddings; MoverScore uses transport-like semantic alignment. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

Lexical metrics penalize valid paraphrases; semantic metrics can overlook changed numbers, negation, or unsupported facts. No single score establishes summary faithfulness. Use multiple references where appropriate, report exact variants/tokenization, and combine automated metrics with source-grounded human or executable checks. Comparing one sentence's BLEU to corpus BLEU is especially misleading.
